title: After the exam
lede: Results arrive faster than most people expect. What to look at, and in what order.

blocks.title: You can see performance within minutes
blocks.text: As soon as students upload their answer files, the assessment overview shows you how the class did. There is no batch process to wait for and nothing OME has to send you.
What to look at, in order

items.d: Distribution and overall performance. Your check that the exam behaved the way you intended.

Find questions the whole class missed, and questions where the distractors did not separate strong students from weak ones. These are your candidates for a scoring adjustment now and for retirement next year.
This is what the tags were for. A report can show category performance as a summary or by exam taker, which tells you whether a topic landed across the cohort.

blocks.title: Talk to OME before adjusting scores
blocks.text: If an item was defective you can accept a second correct answer or drop the item. Do it in consultation with OME rather than on your own, because it changes the record for every student in the cohort.
There is a loop here worth noticing. The item analysis you run this year is what tells you which questions to cut when you duplicate the exam next year. See [Building an assessment](#building).
